title: MQTT Broker Setup & Sensor Network
description: Set up an MQTT broker with multiple simulated IoT sensors publishing temperature, humidity, and pressure data.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Install and configure an MQTT broker (Mosquitto) and create a network of simulated IoT sensors. Configure different QoS levels, topics, and subscriptions for a smart building monitoring system.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Mosquitto MQTT broker
- Python 3.12 with paho-mqtt library
- Working directory: /opt/mqtt-lab

### Tasks
1. Install and configure Mosquitto MQTT broker
2. Set up authentication with username/password
3. Create a temperature sensor publisher script
4. Create a humidity sensor publisher script
5. Create a subscriber that collects all sensor data
6. Configure different QoS levels for different topics
7. Add topic wildcards for monitoring all sensors
8. Create a dashboard showing real-time sensor data

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Mosquitto installed via apt
- Python 3.12 with paho-mqtt
tasks: Install and configure Mosquitto MQTT broker
Set up authentication with username/password
Create a temperature sensor publisher script
Create a humidity sensor publisher script
Create a subscriber that collects all sensor data
Configure different QoS levels for different topics
Add topic wildcards for monitoring all sensors
Create a dashboard showing real-time sensor data

title: Edge Computing with Node-RED
description: Deploy Node-RED for edge computing with data filtering, aggregation, and alert workflows.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Set up Node-RED as an edge computing platform that processes IoT sensor data locally. Create flows for data filtering, aggregation, anomaly detection, and alert notifications.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Node.js 20
- Node-RED installed via npm
- Working directory: /opt/nodered-lab

### Tasks
1. Install and configure Node-RED
2. Create an MQTT input node for sensor data
3. Add function nodes for data validation and filtering
4. Create aggregation flow for 5-minute rolling averages
5. Add threshold alert node for temperature anomalies
6. Create a JSON storage flow for historical data
7. Add a dashboard node for real-time visualization
8. Export the complete Node-RED flow JSON

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Node.js 20 and Node-RED pre-installed
- Node-RED runs on port 1880

Add function nodes for data validation and filtering

title: IoT Security: Device Authentication
description: Implement device authentication using X.509 certificates, secure boot verification, and encrypted communication.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Implement a comprehensive device authentication system using X.509 certificates, mutual TLS authentication, and secure boot verification for IoT devices.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with OpenSSL and Python 3.12
- Certificate authority tools pre-installed
- Working directory: /opt/iot-security-lab

### Tasks
1. Create a Certificate Authority (CA) for device certs
2. Generate device certificates signed by the CA
3. Implement mutual TLS authentication for MQTT
4. Add certificate revocation list (CRL) support
5. Create a device identity verification service
6. Implement secure boot hash verification
7. Add encrypted configuration storage
8. Create an audit log for authentication events

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- OpenSSL and Python 3.12 pre-installed
- Mosquitto with TLS support

title: Embedded Linux: Build Custom Image
description: Build a custom embedded Linux image using Buildroot with custom packages and filesystem configuration.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Create a minimal embedded Linux system using Buildroot. Configure the toolchain, add custom packages, optimize the filesystem for size, and create a bootable image for an IoT gateway device.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with build dependencies
- Buildroot pre-installed
- Working directory: /opt/embedded-linux-lab

### Tasks
1. Initialize a Buildroot project for ARM architecture
2. Configure a minimal Linux kernel
3. Add a custom Python application package
4. Configure networking packages (wpa_supplicant, iptables)
5. Create a root filesystem overlay
6. Optimize image size with package stripping
7. Build the complete firmware image
8. Create a flash and deployment script

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Buildroot and cross-compilation tools installed
- Sufficient disk space for builds

title: MQTT QoS & Retained Messages
description: Master MQTT QoS levels 0, 1, 2 with retained messages, last will, and message persistence.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Explore all three MQTT QoS levels with practical implementations. Understand message delivery guarantees, use retained messages for state storage, and configure last will testament for disconnect notifications.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Mosquitto and Python 3.12
- paho-mqtt library pre-installed
- Working directory: /opt/mqtt-qos-lab

### Tasks
1. Set up Mosquitto with persistence enabled
2. Create QoS 0 publisher and measure delivery
3. Create QoS 1 publisher with acknowledgment
4. Create QoS 2 publisher with exactly-once delivery
5. Configure retained messages for device state topics
6. Set up last will testament for disconnect detection
7. Compare message delivery reliability across QoS levels
8. Create a QoS monitoring dashboard

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Mosquitto and Python 3.12 pre-installed
- Persistence directory configured

title: IoT Data Pipeline to TimescaleDB
description: Build a complete IoT data pipeline from MQTT sensors through Kafka to TimescaleDB for time-series storage.
briefing:

1. Set up MQTT publisher generating sensor data
2. Create a stream processor to validate and transform data
3. Configure TimescaleDB hypertable for time-series data
4. Build the data ingestion pipeline
5. Add data compression and retention policies
6. Create materialized views for common queries
7. Build a monitoring dashboard with Grafana
8. Add alerting for data pipeline failures

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Python 3.12, PostgreSQL 15, TimescaleDB available
- Grafana available for dashboards

title: Digital Twin Simulation
description: Create a digital twin system that simulates a physical IoT device with state synchronization and predictive maintenance.
briefing:

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Python 3.12
- NumPy for simulation
- Working directory: /opt/digital-twin-lab

### Tasks
1. Create a DigitalTwin base class for device simulation
2. Implement a motor simulator with temperature and vibration
3. Add state synchronization between twin and real device
4. Create a failure prediction model using sensor history
5. Build a twin management API for creating and querying twins
6. Add anomaly detection for device behavior
7. Create a 3D visualization of device state
8. Build a predictive maintenance scheduling system

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Python 3.12 with NumPy
- Working directory is empty for fresh setup
